newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ mulls evacuation plan for nationals in PNG.
newsitem.headline: NZ mulls evacuation plan for nationals in PNG.

text.p: New Zealand said on Monday it was working on contingency plans to evacuate its nationals from Papua New Guinea if the Pacific nation's military and political crisis worsened.
Foreign Minister Don McKinnon said he had discussed with Defence Minister Paul East New Zealand's ability to evacuate its citizens from PNG.
He said that although New Zealand had to be prepared to act, relative calm appeared to be holding and there was no immediate concern for people's safety.
"Obviously people are doing some work on this at the present time though I'm not aware that we have lifted to the same level of alert that the Australians have," McKinnon said.

"We haven't got the same logistic capability as Australia but we obviously do have to take into account that if things really deteriorate very badly we do have a responsibility to New Zealand nationals that are in Papua New Guinea at the present time," he added in a radio interview.
Army leaders in PNG have demanded the resignation of Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan in a tense stand-off accompanied in the past week by street violence, riots and looting.
Australia said on Sunday it had placed its defence forces on a higher degree of readiness because of the crisis. About 10,000 Australians and 3,000 New Zealanders live in PNG.
McKinnon said New Zealand's Defence Force would work with Australia's, probably by sending Hercules C130 aircraft, if evacuations became necessary.
